gaps: No independent, non-vendor builder account documenting physical print/assembly friction specific to LeKiwi (tolerance issues, warping, part breakage, heat-set insert problems) was found. The one independent builder account located (Foxglove/Aditya Kamath) reports a smooth physical build with all friction confined to third-party software (a buggy ROS 2 LiDAR driver); this is informative but does not surface print-specific risk. The SIGRobotics-UIUC/LeKiwi GitHub issue tracker was checked directly and has no open or closed issues about print tolerances, part fit, or assembly problems as of this round.

Two community remix files (a Printables 'OmniWheel to Feetech STS3215 Servo Adapter' and a Thingiverse 'Easy OmniWheel to STS3215 adapter hub(s)') surfaced in search results and are plausibly relevant to the research plan's 'community remix used specifically for LeKiwi's base' scope item -- their existence may imply builders needed an alternative to the official wheel-hub-to-servo design -- but both pages returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch, and the agent-browser skill's underlying `belt` CLI is not installed/authenticated in this environment (`belt: command not found`), so the actual reason for each remix (fit issue vs. alternate servo brand vs. preference) could not be confirmed. Flagged as an unconfirmed lead, not a claim.

The $660 LeKiwi headline cost figure from the prior research remains unreconciled against the $482-499 reference BOM. This round adds two new data points -- a $770.47 Dynamixel-variant BOM (higher than $660) and an independent $450-550 estimate from orobot.io (between the two prior figures) -- but per the research plan this reconciliation is explicitly out of bounds unless print-cost-specific evidence resolves it, and it does not; filament/print cost alone is unlikely to close a $160-180 gap and no source prices it out.

This session's WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200 calls) partway through round 2, before a planned search specifically for Reddit/forum/video build-log accounts of LeKiwi print friction could be run. WebFetch remained available and was used for all remaining targeted lookups, but no further WebSearch-driven discovery of new independent sources was possible this round.
summary: Gathered official primary sources for all in-scope research steps: LeKiwi's 3D-printable part files and printer requirements (SIGRobotics-UIUC/LeKiwi repo's 3DPrinting.md: PLA, 15% infill, 0.2mm layers, 150mm/s, ~34hr print time, supports needed on the wheel hub only; SO-101 arm files at TheRobotStudio/SO-ARM100 with bed-size variants, gauge-part testing advice, and no heat-set inserts); a concrete 5-phase assembly sequence with fastener-level detail (Assembly.md); an itemized print-vs-buy BOM confirming the prior research's $482-499 reference figure explicitly excludes print cost, plus a newly-found $770.47 Dynamixel-variant BOM and an independent $450-550 estimate; and the full software/firmware setup phase (install, port-find, motor-setup, two-stage calibration, host/client teleoperation, keyboard speed modes, dataset recording) from the official Hugging Face LeRobot docs. Independent (non-official) corroboration came from the Seeed Studio wiki (assembly phases, print settings, and software-side friction points -- USB permissions, port-detection gotcha, Mac keyboard permission, SSH-not-enabled-by-default), Foxglove/Aditya Kamath's independent builder blog (smooth physical build, friction only in third-party LiDAR software), and orobot.io (independent part-count and cost corroboration). Prior research's established facts (textbook structure, LeKiwi buildability, BOM/cost range, Ch.8 dynamics gap) were cited forward, not re-sourced. Remaining gaps -- lack of independent print-specific friction accounts, two inaccessible community-remix pages, and the still-unreconciled $660 figure -- are reported above rather than silently dropped, consistent with the plan's explicit acceptance of the $660 figure as out of scope to fully resolve.
